etymologies.etymologyHTML: From pre- (“before”) +‎ historic, q.v., similar to slightly earlier ante-historic.

definitions.definition: (properly) Of or relating to the epoch before written record.

quote.text: Was it then in a pre-historic time that the Romans wandered into these lands?

quote.citation: 1981, William Irwin Thompson, The Time Falling Bodies Take to Light: Mythology, Sexuality and the Origins of Culture, London: Rider/Hutchinson & Co., page 137:
quote.text: The cartoon image of prehistoric woman being dragged by the hair by her caveman-husband probably conditions the perceptions of archaeologists far more than they realize.

definitions.definition: (inexact or humorous) Ancient; very old, outdated, etc.
